text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Algeria's Armed Islamic Group (GIA) is seen as threat to European security, says the European Union Council of Justice and Internal Affairs.
- Campaigning for the parliamentary elections in high gear as candidates intensify efforts to win voter support in the last week of the campaign.
- Workers at book printing ENAL company say they have not been paid for eight months.
- Italy's oil firm AGIP said it plans to invest more than $5.0 billion in North Africa to increase its oil reserves in the region.
- Algeria resumes negotiations with the European Union on a trade association deal.
- Security forces kill 120 "terrorists" in the western province of Tissemsilt.
- Algeria's oil and gas Sonatrach company signs a $31.7 million exploration accord with Italian firm Agip.
- Raging contest for parliamentary dominance between National Democratic Rally, grouping government backers, and Islamist-leaning Movement for a Peaceful Society.
